title: The Mont-Blanc Marathon — history and values
claims: The Cross du Mont-Blanc was first held on 1 July 1979 on the initiative of the Club Alpin Francais de Chamonix, then chaired by Georges Costaz and Christian Roussel; 450 participants finished at Planpraz.
In 2003 the race became the Mont-Blanc Marathon, adding a 42 km to the existing 23 km; a 10 km was created afterwards and entries had to be limited from 2010 onwards.
The event added the Kilometre Vertical in 2011, an 80 km in 2013 that later became the 90 km, and the Duo Etoile and Young Race Marathon in 2015.
The history page says the 42 km Mont-Blanc Marathon was part of the Golden Trail World Series from its creation by Salomon in 2018 until 2024.
The event now brings together over 10,000 runners across 8 races in the Mont-Blanc massif.
The Club des Sports de Chamonix was founded in 1905, has 25 sports sections and 4,000 members, and also organises the Kandahar Ski World Cup, the Climbing World Cup and the Mont-Blanc Marathon.
